name: holocron
description: GPU music visualization engine that is also the music player
$licence-note: Holocron is GPL-3.0-or-later (D-010), so GPL dependencies are compatible. What is NOT acceptable is anything non-redistributable: --enable-nonfree FFmpeg stays excluded under any licence. libprojectM at M4 must stay dynamically linked through its C API to keep the LGPL boundary intact (D-012), so it may not simply be added here.
$ffmpeg-note: default-features is FALSE deliberately, and the feature list is explicit. The port's 'gpl' and 'nonfree' features are not in its defaults today, but relying on that is relying on an upstream default we do not control - and 'nonfree' produces libraries that are unredistributable under ANY licence, which would be unfixable after the fact. Listing features also drops avdevice, avfilter and swscale, none of which an audio decoder uses.

$dependency-notes.pocketfft: BSD-3-Clause, header-only. FFT for the analysis stage (#9). The implementation SciPy uses. FFTW was available under D-010 but rejected: a 2048-point real FFT at 93.75 Hz does not justify the weight.
$dependency-notes.libebur128: MIT. ITU-R BS.1770-4 loudness for AudioFrame::loudness_short (#9, D-024). Hand-rolling the K-weighting filter and gating would produce a number that looks plausible and is not comparable across tracks, which would destroy the only reason D-007 leaves the field un-normalized.
$dependency-notes.catch2: BSL-1.0, GPL-compatible. Test-only, hence the feature.
$dependency-notes.tomlplusplus: MIT, header-only. Crystal manifests (M2), and gatekeeper.toml when a loader exists. TOML rather than JSON because these files are edited by hand by crystal authors: comments survive, trailing commas are not an error, and a typo in a key is a parse error at a named line rather than a silently-ignored member.
$dependency-notes.glad: MIT. The GL function loader for the 4.5 core context (D-012). Issue #13 proposed committing glad2's generated output under third_party/ to avoid version drift; the manifest gets the same guarantee -- glad is pinned by the same builtin-baseline as everything else and moves only when the baseline does -- without carrying generated code in the tree. Features are explicit: 'loader' and 'gl-api-45', so nothing above 4.5 is even declared and a 4.6-only call is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise on a lesser GPU.
$dependency-notes.sdl3: Zlib AND MIT AND Apache-2.0, GPL-compatible. The first sink backend (#1) and, later, the window and GL 4.5 context. default-features is FALSE, which costs nothing on the target: every one of the port's default features (ibus, wayland, x11) is platform-gated to Linux, so Windows resolves to the same set either way. Turning them off spares the Linux CI job a chain of system dev packages for a platform that is a second compiler, not a deployment target (D-022). SDL's built-in dummy audio driver needs no feature and no hardware, which is how the sink is exercised headless on both platforms.
